instructions: Fill every item after the two-stage audit. Preserve your blind answer. Allowed verdicts: accept, revise, reject, unverifiable. No default acceptance. Nulls must be completed, or explicitly describe unavailable information. Cite sourceId and line ranges. Return this JSON plus a concise overall summary. This is an audit response, not an importable review package.
rubric: correct answer and source support under the stated version

items.rationale: Key correct. Only Data Zone Standard combines data-zone processing with pay-per-token billing; Global = any region, Data Zone Provisioned = reserved PTU, Data Zone Batch = async. All option notes supported.

sourceEvidence.supports: Global any region; Data Zone within US/EU/APAC zone

issues: Minor wording: explanation says 'selected data zone'; S005:24 says 'Microsoft-specified data zone'.

Answer leakage from case wording: 'EU data zone', 'pay-per-token', 'without reserving throughput units' and 'batch unsuitable' map one-to-one onto the option names, so the item is recall of the table rather than a decision.
items.suggestedCorrection: None required for correctness; see difficultyAssessment for optional discrimination changes.
items.difficultyAssessment: Provisional medium; assessed easy-to-medium. To raise discrimination, describe requirements in business terms (e.g. 'EU customers; processing may cross EU countries but not leave the EU; spiky traffic; finance rejects monthly capacity commitments') and add Standard (geography) as an option so the candidate must separate data zone from geography.

items.rationale: Key D correct: private networking excludes key auth (S040:5); keyless setup uses the containing Foundry account's system-assigned identity with Search Index Data Contributor + Search Service Contributor (S040:45-47, 887-891). sourceEvidence.supports: key-based auth not supported with private VNet
account system-assigned MI + two Search roles
provisioning caller vs runtime identity distinction

issues: Unsupported claim: option C note says 'Foundry User is a project role'. No excerpt mentions Foundry User. C is still wrong (Search Index Data Contributor missing), but the note asserts an unevidenced fact.
Stem says 'documented retrieval problem', but the case documents no failure symptom (no 403, no empty results); it only lists configuration facts.

Source tension: S040:5 and S011:74 say 'project managed identity'; S040:45 names the account's system-assigned identity. The case resolves this by stipulation ('For this setup'), which is acceptable but is a stipulated, not documented, reconciliation.
Heavy leakage: the case names the correct principal and states the exact missing role, so A, B and C are eliminated by the case text alone.
Case-child coupling: shared case text says 'deployment types listed in Q1', so the shared context refers to a sibling item.
items.suggestedCorrection: Stem: 'Which connection and authorization change lets the agent query the index while preserving the case study's network and runtime-identity requirements?' Option C note: 'C does not grant Search Index Data Contributor, which the keyless setup requires (S040:45-47).' Drop the Foundry User claim or add a source. Optionally give a symptom (e.g. agent Search tool calls return 403 after switching to keyless) instead of stating the missing role.
items.difficultyAssessment: Provisional very_hard; assessed medium as written, because the case states the principal and the missing role. It can reach hard if the case gives only the symptom and current role list, and the options vary identity and role independently (e.g. account MI + Search Index Data Reader; project MI + Index Data Contributor).

overall.summary: Blind answers matched the author key on all ten items, and the key is correct on all ten under the frozen snapshots. No reject. Two revise: Q2 (unsupported 'Foundry User is a project role' note; stem cites a retrieval problem the case never documents) and Q7 (group R log says retries already fail, which undermines key option E). Eight accept. Main weakness is difficulty: stems and case text name the answer, so 6 of 10 items are easier than labelled. No Azure execution performed; snapshot files beyond file 02 were not opened.
overall.releaseRecommendation: Do not release revision 1. Apply the Q2 and Q7 corrections, recalibrate difficulty labels, add the missing S037 locator lines, then request a new bound review for changed items (and for Q1, because a shared-case edit invalidates both children).

difficultyAndCoverageFindings: Assessed difficulty vs provisional: Q1 easy-medium (medium), Q2 medium (very_hard), Q3 medium (very_hard), Q4 easy-medium (hard), Q5 medium (medium), Q6 easy (hard), Q7 medium-hard after fix (hard), Q8 easy-medium (medium), Q9 easy (medium), Q10 medium (hard). Recurring cause: requirements are phrased with the same nouns as the correct option, and distractors violate an explicit constraint in the stem. Stronger items state business requirements and symptoms and make the candidate translate them.
Domain mix 3/3/2/1/1 vs official AI-103 weights (study guide updated 2026-04-14: A 25-30%, B 30-35%, C/D/E 10-15% each): C is slightly over-weighted at 20%; acceptable for a 10-item pilot.

Case study: Microsoft describes case studies as complex scenarios that test identifying critical information and synthesizing it (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/credentials/certifications/frequently-asked-questions). The Cedar Atlas case states the critical facts directly. No Microsoft primary source found that quantifies case-study length.

verdictConvention: Verdicts judge the bound item content (stem, options, key, explanations). Difficulty relabels are reported in difficultyAssessment and overall findings; applying one changes the item hash and needs a new bound review.
